column1: # G6 phases 0-1: the HASH FORM and the canon-hash
# hcanon -- hcanon(unify(src)): exactly the unify-level canon with the
# two additions that close its semantic gaps, a closed map or list
# wrapped as close({...}) / close([...]) and the type/hide marks
# rendered as type(x) / hide(x). Both reuse parseable syntax, so the
# hash form is valid aontu source; every hcanon row additionally
# asserts the ROUND-TRIP property that makes the hash meaningful,
# canon -- the same sources under the USER-FACING canon, which G6 does
# not change. These rows sit beside their hcanon twins so the
# difference is the readable pin: canon drops closedness and marks,
# UTF-8(hcanon(v)))) pin, asserted byte-for-byte in both ports.
# The marks propagate to every descendant at unification, so a wrapper
# is emitted only where a mark STARTS (hcanon-hide-leaf-only,
# hcanon-all-wrappers-one-value). Every expectation was obtained by
# the parity probe (AGENTS.md): both engines were run over this corpus
